Let me understand the rule.

Input is a 5x1 grid (1 row, 5 columns). Number of non-zero (colored) dots = c. Output size = (c*5) x (c*5)? Wait "height and width will be the number of colored dots times 5". So N = c*5 rows and N columns.

Pattern: copy input pattern to bottom-left corner. Next row up copy shifted right by 1 block... wait "move it to the right by 1 block" - block meaning 1 cell? Let's check example.

Input: [0,0,0,6,0], colored dots = 1 (one 6). N = 5. Output 5x5.

Bottom row: [0,0,0,6,0] copied at bottom-left (rows... it's a single row pattern). Row 4 (bottom): [0,0,0,6,0] matching input.

Row 3: shifted right by 1? Input pattern [0,0,0,6,0] shifted right by 1 would be [.,0,0,0,6,0] -> [0,0,0,0,6]? Actually shifting right by 1: position of 6 at index 3 -> index 4. So [0,0,0,0,6]. But example row 3 is [0,0,0,0,0] and row 4 is [0,0,0,0,6], wait let me re-read.

Output:
row0: 0 0 0 0 0
row1: 0 0 0 0 0
row2: 0 0 0 0 0
row3: 0 0 0 0 6
row4: 0 0 0 6 0

Hmm, bottom row (row4) has 6 at index 3 (same as input). Row3 has 6 at index 4 (shifted right by 1). Rows above: 6 would be at index 5 (off grid) so all zeros.

So it's like a diagonal line going up-right from the bottom-left. Actually the copy is placed at bottom, then each row up shifts right by 1. But wait it's "copy pattern to bottom left, next row up copy shifted right by 1 block".

Hmm actually with the 6 at index 3, shifting up and right means it goes off grid after 1. Yes.

Now the verifier: let's decode.

x0 = asobject(I) -> set of (value, (i,j)).
x1 = matcher(first, ZERO) -> function checking value==0.
x2 = compose(flip, x1) -> not zero, i.e., colored.
x3 = sfilter(x0, x2) -> colored cells.
x4 = size(x3) -> number colored cells = c (assuming all distinct).
x5 = width(I) = 5.
x6 = multiply(x5, x4) = 5c = N.
x7 = multiply(UNITY, x6) = (N, N).
x8 = canvas(ZERO, (N,N)) -> NxN zeros.
x9 = multiply(x5,x4) = N.
x10 = decrement(x9) = N-1.
x11 = lbind(astuple, x10) -> lambda y: (N-1, y).
x12 = rbind(shoot, UP_RIGHT) -> lambda start: shoot(start, (-1,1)).
x13 = compose(last, last) -> for a cell (value,(i,j)), last gives (i,j), last again gives j.
x14 = chain(x12, x11, x13) -> lambda cell: x12(x11(x13(cell))) = shoot((N-1, j), (-1,1)). So from row N-1, column j, shoot in direction up-right: cells (N-1-k, j+k).

x15 = fork(recolor, first, x14) -> lambda cell: recolor(value, x14(cell)): the line with color = value.

x16 = mapply(x15, x3) -> all lines merged.

x17 = paint(x8, x16).

So the bottom row is row N-1: cell at (N-1, j) for each colored cell at column j in input.

Wait input is 1 row, 5 columns. The colored cells are at (0, j) with value. The line start is (N-1, j). So indeed the pattern is copied to bottom row with same columns, then diagonal up-right.

But note: if input had multiple colored cells, c counts them. N = c*5.

Now my given input: [[0,6,7,8,9]]. Colored cells: values 6,7,8,9 at columns 1,2,3,4. c=4. N=20. Output 20x20.

Bottom row (row 19): 0 6 7 8 9 at columns 1,2,3,4.
Row 18: shifted right: 6 at col2, 7 at col3, 8 at col4, 9 at col5.
Row 17: 6 at col3, 7 col4, 8 col5, 9 col6.
... continue until row where columns exceed 19.

Row 19-k has colored at columns 1+k, 2+k, 3+k, 4+k (for each, if within 0..19).

Let's compute rows from top: row index i, then k = 19 - i. Columns = 1+k, 2+k, 3+k, 4+k = 20-i, 21-i, 22-i, 23-i. Wait 1+19-i = 20-i.

Hmm for i=19 (bottom): k=0, columns 1,2,3,4. Good.
For i=18: k=1, cols 2,3,4,5.
...
For i=3: k=16, cols 17,18,19,20 -> 20 out of range (max index 19). So cols 17,18,19.
i=2: k=17, cols 18,19,20,21 -> 18,19.
i=1: k=18, cols 19,20,... -> 19.
i=0: k=19, cols 20,... -> none.

Let me just compute per row i from 0 to 19:
k = 19 - i.
Columns with colors: for each colored input at column j (j=1,2,3,4 with values 6,7,8,9):
col = j + k = j + 19 - i.
Value = 6 if j=1, 7 if j=2, 8 if j=3, 9 if j=4.
Include if 0 <= col <= 19.

So row i: col j+19-i.

For i, columns range 1+19-i to 4+19-i = 20-i to 23-i.

Need col <= 19: 20-i <= 19 -> i>=1. For i=1: cols 19,20,21,22 -> only 19 (j=1, value 6). 
i=2: cols 18,19,20,21 -> 18(j=1,6), 19(j=2,7).
i=3: cols 17,18,19,20 -> 17(6),18(7),19(8).
i=4: 16,17,18,19 -> 16(6),17(7),18(8),19(9).
i>=4: all 4 present.

i=0: cols 20,21,22,23 -> none.

So rows 0: all zeros.
Row 1: col19=6.
Row 2: col18=6, col19=7.
Row 3: col17=6, col18=7, col19=8.
Row 4: col16=6,col17=7,col18=8,col19=9.
Row 5: col15=6,col16=7,col17=8,col18=9.
...
Row 19: col1=6,col2=7,col3=8,col4=9.

Pattern: for row i>=4, cols 20-i..23-i with values 6,7,8,9 respectively. Actually col = j+19-i, for j=1..4: values 6,7,8,9.

Let me build 20x20 grid.

Row i, columns 0-19.

i=0: all 0.
i=1: col19=6 -> [0]*19 + [6]
i=2: col18=6, col19=7 -> [0]*18 + [6,7]
i=3: col17=6,18=7,19=8 -> [0]*17 + [6,7,8]

i=5: col15=6,16=7,17=8,18=9 -> [0]*15 + [6,7,8,9] then col19=0
Wait: cols 15,16,17,18. So [0]*15 + [6,7,8,9] + [0]*1. Length = 15+4+1=20. Good.
i=6: cols 14,15,16,17 -> [0]*14+[6,7,8,9]+[0]*2.
...
General i>=4: cols 20-i, 21-i, 22-i, 23-i. So prefix zeros count = 20-i. Then values 6,7,8,9, then suffix zeros = 19-(23-i) = i-4. Check i=4: prefix=16, suffix=0. Good. i=19: prefix=1, suffix=15. So [0,6,7,8,9,0...15]. Bottom row col1=6,...col4=9. Good matches.

Now compose all rows.

Rows:
